player_intent: Every real pistol, assault rifle, and submachine gun equips at human scale and remains visibly connected to its trigger and support hands with the same stable ready and fire-recovery quality as the Mark 23.
acceptance_rule: Through res://main.tscn, each in-scope firearm resolves exactly one published model-specific visual rig or its existing authored weapon rig before mesh, animation-family, and hand-contact consumers run. Pistols resolve TWO_HAND_PISTOL, rifles and SMGs resolve their rifle family, every resolved mesh has human-scale geometry and seven physical sockets, the right hand remains the sole weapon-root owner, and only the left support hand solves to the weapon. In ordinary Ready Aim and accepted-shot recovery, every pistol's projected optic-up axis remains within 12 degrees of operator up, both palms remain within 1 cm of their physical contacts, and the bore remains within 1 degree of camera-owned aim. Accepted standing and crouched shots retain the existing posture-matched 1.2-second FIRE_RECOVERY without a separate fire OneShot. Designator, air_to_ground_missile, and exploding_fuel are excluded because their catalog records are not handheld firearms.

nodes.role: Keeps exactly one rigid weapon root attached to the live operator trigger hand while model-specific sockets remain presentation data.
Closes only the support palm onto the published physical foregrip without moving the weapon, trigger shoulder, torso, or gameplay aim.

must_not_change: CharacterBody3D movement, posture, collision, and movement-tech authority
SOCOM camera and reticle aim-intent authority
server shot validation, muzzle authority, ballistics, damage, ammunition, and networking
the existing 1.2-second accepted-shot recovery and no-fire-OneShot behavior
right trigger-hand attachment as the sole weapon-root transform owner
existing authored Mark 23, AK-47, M4A1, AssaultRifle_1, M16A2, and M40A1 geometry
visual_check: Launch res://main.tscn and cycle the pistol, assault-rifle, and SMG catalog in standing ready, crouched ready, standing recovery, and crouched recovery. Each real gun must be human-sized, remain rigidly owned by the trigger hand, keep the left palm on its physical support contact, point its bore toward the camera-owned reticle, retain square shoulders, and never select an AGLS pose strip or recoil clip as the base fire state.

system_delta.reason: Keep the proven family animation and 1.2-second FIRE_RECOVERY owners, but replace legacy scale-one meshes and generic sockets with immutable per-model visual rigs resolved once for runtime and editor consumers. The first published pistol rigs are replaced by revision-2 rigs because canonical rendered evidence measured an approximately 90-degree axial roll even though bore and palm metrics passed; revision 2 adds the certified 90-degree grip-axis correction and a direct rendered roll guard. Direct AGLS pose strips and recoil are rejected here because measured retargeting introduces large hand and shoulder displacement; AGLS aim sweep and recoil 02 remain separate additive experiments.

current.system: Complete family animation routing paired with sparse catalog geometry, generic in-memory socket fallbacks, and pistol rigs lacking an optic-up axial-roll check

candidate.system: Published per-model family visual rigs, including revision-2 upright pistol grips, resolved by the shared weapon contract and guarded by canonical rendered contact, aim, and axial-roll evidence
